title: Sheet
description: A bare rounded screen with the front of a record sleeve on it, the cover and then title, artist, year and side one set label against value on one axis, and a bottom sheet that is the back of the same sleeve: its head is side two's first row, "Side two" against "Here Comes the Sun 3:05", set exactly like the side one rows above it, so at rest the sheet reads as the page's listing carrying on. Half stops one empty line under side one's total, measured off the page, so the whole of side one, its tabular times and its total sit in view directly over side two. Drag the sheet up and the record turns over: side one steps back the way an iOS page does, scaling to 0.94, rounding its corners and dimming a little, all in step with your finger, while side two rises to fill the screen with the rest of its titles and total, the label, and the song's credits set name against part on the same axis. Titles that turn over hang and carry their running time down to the last line. The clock is set twice and cut along the page's edge as it moves, white over the black and ink over the page, so it is never half on the wrong ground. The drag follows the finger exactly; let go and the speed is projected forward to choose peek, half or full, then a spring carries it in, and you can catch it mid-flight. Past full it rubber-bands. At full the credits scroll, and a drag that scrolls them back to the top keeps going and pulls the sheet down in the same gesture. A click on the head steps up, Escape and the arrow keys step through the detents.
intent: The motion is Emil Kowalski's Vaul drawer and iOS sheets with detents: the drag follows the pointer one to one, release velocity picks the detent, damping past the edge instead of a hard stop, the presenting page scaling back with rounded corners, and scroll handing off to the drag only at the top. The phone is reduced to its glass so none of that has to compete with a mock of iOS; what the sheet carries instead is a 1969 credit block, typeset on a centred axis the way record sleeves and film titles set name against role.
